title: The ram and the goat (Dan 8)

symbols.symbol: Ram with two horns, the higher coming up last
Male goat from the west, not touching the ground
Great horn between the goat's eyes, broken at its height
symbols.in_text_interpretation: "The first king" of Greece (8:21); not named.

symbols.symbol: Four notable horns toward the four winds
symbols.description: Rise in place of the great horn
symbols.in_text_interpretation: "Four kingdoms will stand up out of the nation, but not with his power" (8:22); not named.

symbols.symbol: Little horn from one of the four
symbols.description: Grows toward the south, the east and the glorious land; casts down host and stars; removes the continual offering; casts down the sanctuary
symbols.in_text_interpretation: "A king of fierce face" in the latter time of their kingdom (8:23–25); not named.

symbols.description: Against whom the horn magnifies itself
symbols.in_text_interpretation: "The prince of princes" (8:25); not further identified.
"The vision of the evenings and mornings … is true" and belongs to many days to come (8:26); the unit is not explained.

description: A ram, a goat, four horns and a little horn that attacks the host of heaven and the sanctuary, interpreted by Gabriel. Unlike ch. 7, the text itself names Media, Persia and Greece; later identifications (Alexander, the successors, Antiochus) are interpretations recorded on the prophecy records.
